_doc: Chart event markers. Dates are UTC days and each is the date of the cited source itself (`verified: direct`). A date that can only be derived is not placed on a chart: see `not_marked`. site/data/events.json carries date and label only.

events.label: Swaps launch
events.evidence: Variational, 2026-09-01T19:33:28Z: 'The first swap markets ($XAU and $US100) are now live on Omni.'

events.label: Binance hack
events.evidence: Variational, 2026-10-29T21:12:20Z: 'On the possible Binance hack: All user funds on Omni are safe.' The post dates Variational's response; it words the event as possible.

events.label: Public mainnet
events.evidence: Variational, 2026-11-11T15:31:45Z: 'The Omni Private Beta has ended. The platform is now live in Public Mainnet.' The linked X post (status 2120538337815736402) was created 2026-11-11T15:25:12Z. That is 12 Nov in Korea; the UTC day is 11 Nov.

not_marked.label: First RWA perpetuals
not_marked.reason: No post is dated to the first listing. Counting back from two later posts gives 2026-05-20, which is derived, so it is not marked.
not_marked.evidence: Variational, 2026-06-09T13:49Z: '$MU is the 21st RWA listing on Variational over the past 20 days' (9 Jun minus 20 days). Same count-back from https://t.me/variational_io/322, 2026-06-11T14:37Z: '26 new RWA listings over the past 22 days'. The biweekly update of 2026-05-29 (https://t.me/variational_io/317) records 'Listed initial RWA markets'. No post dated to the first listing itself is in the channel.
